newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex lira bond seen benefitting on positive view.
newsitem.headline: Pemex lira bond seen benefitting on positive view.

text.p: Mexican oil giant Petroleos Mexicanos' (Pemex) latest bond issue has benefitted from the perception that Latin American oil companies are a better bet than sovereigns, analysts said on Wednesday.
State-owned Pemex said it placed a seven-year 350 billion floating-rate lira issue with a coupon of 165 basis points over three month Libor, and a yield of 169.8 basis points over.
"Typically issuers like Pemex tend to trade rich to the sovereign issues," said Bear, Stearns debt analyst Tulio Vera.
"There is a perception that oil companies are somewhat better credit risks than sovereigns," he said, adding he did not necessarily agree with the perception.
Long-term Pemex bonds are trading tighter than longer-term Mexican federal government bonds, analysts said.
The latest Pemex issue, worth about $207 million, was placed mostly in the Italian market, but to a lesser extent in Switzerland, Spain, Luxembourg, and in Asia.
"The issue was particularly well received by Italian institutional investors," Pemex said in a statement.
Pemex and other oil companies benefit from having most of their revenues denominated in U.S. dollars.
Pemex has made earlier visits to the Italian lira market.
The last time was in April last year, it placed a two-year 300 billion lira note, worth about $192.6 million.
By turning again to lira, Pemex says it is diversifying its financing sources. It is also taking advantage of strong demand for Mexican paper.

In January, for example, the United Mexican States, the formal name for the federal government, placed a 10-year 500 billion lira issue, at 232 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. That followed a five-year UMS issue in the same market last November.
Pemex is also following other Mexican borrowers in lengthening the maturities of its debt.
The company also has a strategy of moving to medium-term paper, from the two and three-year maturities it placed in 1996.
Pemex plans to place three debt issues in total in 1997, totalling $800 million, officials said recently.
The oil giant placed three bonds in 1996, after staying away from international capital market in 1995.
Pemex has also been considering a $250 million five-year Eurobond, possibly led by SBC Warburg. The company is also said to be considering a yen issue.
The latest lira issue was led by J.P. Morgan and Banca Commerciale Italiana, as well as Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and CABOTO. The syndicate was also made up of 21 other institutes, Pemex said.
